newsitem.title: SPAIN: Telefonica aims to be among market leaders.
newsitem.headline: Telefonica aims to be among market leaders.

text.p: Spain's Telefonica chairman, Juan Villalonga, said on Friday he was confident the telecommunications firm would be among the top five or six leading companies worldwide in the industry in the future.

"Our future project is to become one out of the five or six biggest (world) operators after a consolidation process which will cut sharply the current number of global operators," Villalonga told a shareholders meeting.
To reach this target, Telefonica must strengthen itself in existing markets and start up new business, he said.
Telefonica wants to develop its multimedia business and to enter new markets. It is aiming for the Spanish-speaking markets in the U.S. and the Asian market.
Villalonga was also in favour of early privatisation in the industry, which could be brought forward to January 1 1998 instead of December 1998 as planned.
During 1996 Telefonica cut its international tariffs by an average 25 percent and recently lowered them by another 8.8 percent.

The company has proposed a reduction in the cost of inter-regional calls in Spain and it is prepared to cut, if regulatory authorities approve, the tariffs charged by its analogue technology mobile telephone company Moviline.
